prompt: Which description sounds most like your marketing right now?

options.text: We’re doing plenty, but I’m not always confident we’re working on the right things.
We get interest, but our follow-up and nurturing could be much more consistent.
We do good work, but not enough of the right people are finding us or seeing what makes us different.
People are finding us, but too few are taking the next step and becoming qualified inquiries or clients.
Marketing gets done, but I’m still the person keeping most of it moving.

prompt: What usually happens to marketing when the business gets really busy?

options.text: We become reactive and whatever feels most urgent becomes the priority.
Follow-up, email, and lead nurturing become inconsistent.
Content, SEO, outreach, or other visibility work slows down.
We keep marketing, but rarely have time to look at what is converting and improve it.
A lot of marketing slows down or stops because I no longer have time to direct it.

prompt: Which best describes how marketing gets planned in your business?

options.text: We have lots of ideas, but deciding what deserves attention first is difficult.
We plan ways to attract interest, but what happens after someone becomes a lead is less organized.
We know we need to stay visible, but creating and distributing trust-building content consistently is a challenge.
We plan marketing activity, but conversion, customer journey, and sales outcomes aren’t always part of the conversation.
Most of the plan still lives in my head, and other people wait for my direction.

prompt: Imagine a promising potential client discovers your business today. What is most likely to get in their way?

options.text: Our messaging, offers, or priorities aren’t always connected enough to give them one clear story.
They may show interest, but what happens afterward depends too much on manual follow-up.
They may not find enough useful content, proof, expertise, or visibility to build trust in the first place.
They can find us and understand us, but the path to booking, inquiring, or buying has friction.
Moving them forward often requires me to personally step in, respond, approve something, or tell the team what to do.

prompt: Which statement is closest to how you feel about your marketing performance?

options.text: We have data and ideas, but deciding what deserves our attention next is the hard part.
I don’t have a clear picture of what happens to leads between initial interest and a sales conversation.
We need a stronger and more consistent flow of the right people discovering the business.
We get attention or traffic, but I’m not confident enough of it turns into qualified business.
Even when we have reporting or data, I’m usually the one who has to figure out what everyone should do with it.

prompt: Imagine your qualified website traffic doubled next month. What would most likely happen?

options.text: More traffic would be nice, but we’d still need to decide what we’re actually trying to move people toward.
We’d get more leads, but our nurture and follow-up systems probably wouldn’t keep up.
That would address a major part of our current problem. We need more of the right people finding us.
I’m not convinced twice the traffic would mean twice the inquiries. Something in the conversion journey still needs work.
More marketing activity would probably create more things for me to monitor, approve, or coordinate.

prompt: Which change would feel like the biggest relief right now?

options.text: Knowing exactly what our marketing priorities are and what we can safely ignore.
Knowing leads are being followed up with and nurtured without relying on someone’s memory.
Knowing the right people are consistently discovering us and seeing why they should trust us.
Knowing our website and customer journey are doing a better job turning interest into real opportunities.
Knowing marketing will continue moving even when I’m focused on clients, operations, or the rest of the business.

prompt: Who is currently responsible for making sure the whole marketing system works together?

options.text: We have people doing pieces of marketing, but nobody clearly owns overall priorities and direction.
Different people or tools handle leads and communication, but nobody fully owns the nurture and follow-up journey.
Visibility work is spread across content, website, SEO, social, referrals, or other channels without one person connecting it.
We have marketing activity, but nobody consistently owns conversion, customer journey, reporting, and optimization.
Me. Even when other people help execute, I’m still the person ultimately connecting all the dots.
